Multiple bird strikes during descent.
The failure of the ACA795 flight crew to monitor and/or switch to the appropriate air traffic control frequency.
The student pilot's improper use of the airbrakes while on approach for landing.

The pilot's misjudged distance/altitude which resulted in an undershoot while on final approach to land. Factors contributing to the accident were the lack of thermal lift (sinking air), and the lack of suitable terrain for the off-airport landing.
The pilot's failure to maintain clearance from a tree while making an off-field landing in a glider. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's inadequate compensation for the gusting winds.
The pilot's failure to attain the proper glide path and the flight instructor's delayed remedial action. Contributing to the accident was the encountered headwind.
A loss of engine power due to fuel exhaustion, and the pilot’s failure to ensure that a sufficient quantity of fuel was on board to complete the flight.
The student pilot’s failure to maintain directional control during the landing with gusty wind conditions.
The loss of engine power for an undetermined reason. A factor was the berm encountered during the forced landing.

The pilot’s failure to maintain adequate airspeed and his exceedance of the airplane’s critical angle-of-attack, which resulted in an aerodynamic stall. Contributing to the accident was the pilot’s failure to retract the flaps after beginning the go-around.

The pilot’s failure to maintain adequate airspeed while maneuvering at a low altitude in high density altitude conditions, which resulted in the airplane’s inability to climb or maintain clearance from terrain.

A loss of engine power that resulted from fuel contamination when it was treated with a 70% isopropyl alcohol solution (antiseptic) that contained water. Contributing to the accident were vague fuel treatment instructions provided by the operator.
The non-instrument-rated pilot's decision to fly into known instrument meteorological conditions, which resulted in the pilot's spatial disorientation and loss of airplane control.

The pilot's improper decision to take off with the airplane at a high gross weight from a short, turf runway, which degraded its climb performance and led to a delayed aborted takeoff, a runway excursion, and impact with terrain.

The pilot's use of an alternate traffic pattern entry procedure, which resulted in his inability to see and avoid the other airplane, which was flying the preferred traffic pattern, and the subsequent midair collision.
The pilot’s failure to extend the landing gear during the approach to land.
The pilot’s failure to properly monitor the flight controls (toe brake pedals) during engine start.

The flight instructor’s failure to raise the landing gear using the alternate system, which resulted in a reduced climb rate and impact with an obstacle. Contributing to the accident was the flight instructor’s lack of understanding of the backup landing gear extender system.
The pilot's failure to attain adequate airspeed before attempting the takeoff with a tailwind, which resulted in the airplane being unable to sustain flight.

The pilot’s failure to attain a proper glidepath on approach for landing, which resulted in impact with trees. The pilot's loss of control due to spatial disorientation while flying in instrument meteorological conditions. Contributing to the accident was the failure of the vacuum pump and its associated instruments.
The pilot's incorrect altimeter setting during the night visual approach, which resulted in a controlled flight into terrain.
Undetermined due to lack of available evidence.

incidents.cause: Maintenance personnel's inadequate inspection of the oil system's fittings during a routine oil servicing, which resulted in oil starvation due to a loose and/or detached oil line B-nut fitting that led to the engine seizing while in flight.
The student pilot’s improper flare.

The pilot’s failure to comply with the manufacturer’s limitations and guidance regarding flaperons usage at low altitude and in adverse wind conditions, which resulted in an in-flight loss of airplane control.
The pilot's failure to maintain clearance from the wire.
The pilot's diverted attention during an agricultural application maneuver, which resulted in the helicopter impacting a corn field.
The pilot's failure to maintain adequate skid clearance from the helicopter cart during landing, resulting in a dynamic rollover.

The flight instructor’s failure to verify that the left engine was operational, which resulted in insufficient engine power being available during an attempted go-around and his subsequent loss of airplane control. The pilot's misjudged approach which resulted in overshooting the landing point and insufficient remaining landing surface.

The pilot's decision to land with insufficient obstacle clearance.

The pilot's failure to maintain directional control after landing resulting in a collision with terrain.
The pilot's loss of directional control during takeoff in gusty crosswind conditions.
The pilot's and flight instructor's improper brake application during the landing roll. Contributing to the accident was the flight instructor's failure to make a positive transfer of controls.
The pilot's failure to confirm the flaps had been retracted during takeoff, which resulted in a loss of lift and subsequent collision with terrain.
The pilot's loss of directional control during takeoff, resulting in a collision with terrain and ground loop.
The pilot's failure to maintain control of the airplane while taking off with a gusting crosswind.
The failure of the pilot receiving instruction to maintain directional control during the landing roll, resulting in a ground-loop.
The pilot's failure to see and avoid a power line during an agricultural application flight.

The pilot's improper decision to maneuver at a low altitude and in close proximity to a wind turbine undergoing maintenance, which resulted in a collision with a tagline rope being held by a worker on the ground and serious injury to the worker.
The pilot's failure to maintain clearance from a telephone pole during an agricultural application flight.
The pilot's failure to maintain clearance from wires during an agricultural application flight.

The pilot’s selection of unsuitable terrain for landing in crosswind conditions, which resulted in the airplane inadvertently becoming airborne and a subsequent hard landing and loss of directional control.
The pilot’s failure to maintain clearance from power transmission lines during low altitude flight operations. Contributing to the accident was the pilot’s impairment due to a sedating medication.
The pilot did not maintain adequate clearance from tree, which resulted in a collision with a tree and subsequent impact with terrain.
